name: agent-dispatch-recipe-loops-eval
description: Tier-E (agent-driven) live-forge doc-audit of agent-dispatch's four named global recipes (backlog-triager, issue-reproducer, effort-builder, effort-driver): install agent-dispatch PLUS its two genuine documented headless-embody runtime dependencies (agent-bridge, agent-worktrees) on a fresh box, clone a REAL (operator-supplied, scratch, not-this-repo) GitHub repository that already carries the four recipe declarations under its own .copilot-extensions/agent-dispatch/registrar/ plus real fixture issues/efforts, then drive a FRESH in-container Copilot session under LITERAL MODE as the ORCHESTRATOR: register the repo, let the declared cadence tick the real coordinator, and supervise/observe -- never itself perform the recipe work. Each loop's own headless worker is a separate Copilot process agent-dispatch itself spawns; the orchestrator's job is only registration, discovery, and reporting real terminal task state plus real GitHub-side evidence. Judges whether repository-issue-loop-adoption.md + repository-issue-loop.md's Operations section (plus the README's recipe table, for the un-dedicated effort-driver-loop CLI path) let a fresh agent operate all four recipes live, end to end, with no self-repair. Name-free / public: the fixture repository identity and forge login are supplied entirely via REQUIRED env (CR_FIXTURE_REPO, CR_FIXTURE_PRODUCER_LOGIN), never hardcoded here -- a consuming harness supplies its own scratch fixture repo via -PassEnv or equivalent.

auth.gh: required (forwarded from the same injected Copilot token account)

starting_state.notes: agent-dispatch, agent-bridge, AND agent-worktrees installed and first-session-provisioned (binstubs on PATH) -- agent-bridge and agent-worktrees are genuine documented runtime dependencies of headless embody (spawn-supervisor.md: a headless lane's default --headless-agent 'task-worker' must be registered with agent-bridge on the host; embody.py's create_worktree() always shells out to `agent-worktrees create`), not incidental extras; gh CLI installed and authenticated from the SAME injected COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN (run.ps1 -TokenAccount <acct> already mints this as that account's own `gh auth token`, so no separate -PassEnv is needed) via a persisted `gh auth login --with-token` credential (an env-var export alone would not survive into the orchestrator's own separate `docker exec` tool calls); the real fixture repo named by $CR_FIXTURE_REPO cloned to ~/recipe-fixture (it already carries the four recipe declarations under .copilot-extensions/agent-dispatch/registrar/ plus real fixture issues/efforts -- setup.sh does NOT author or mutate any of that content, only clones it); the fixture repo is registered as an agent-worktrees project and a local 'task-worker' agent-bridge venue is registered (both host-level topology, analogous to a real deployment's already-adopted projects.yaml/machines.yaml/acp-agents.json); the singleton supervisor daemon (`agent-dispatch supervise serve`) is started here as pre-existing HOST INFRASTRUCTURE -- on a real deployed host this is a long-running systemd --user service installed once, well before any adopter ever runs `repository-issue-loop setup`, and this container has no systemd to install that service into, so setup.sh stands in for it rather than asking the orchestrator to discover/bootstrap it itself; the local coordinator is NOT pre-registered with the repo -- that registration is itself part of what this eval audits.

prompt: You are the ORCHESTRATOR for a live agent-dispatch repository-issue-loop + effort-driver-loop validation against a REAL GitHub repository checked out at this cwd (its own git remote names the real repo -- read it, never assume a name). This checkout already carries four recipe declarations under .copilot-extensions/agent-dispatch/registrar/ (backlog-triager.yaml, issue-reproducer.yaml, effort-builder.yaml, effort-driver.yaml) and real, already-filed GitHub issues/efforts for each. Your job is ONLY to register, supervise, and observe these four loops using agent-dispatch's own documented CLI -- never to triage issues, reproduce bugs, build efforts, or drive effort work yourself; each loop's own headless worker is a SEPARATE Copilot process agent-dispatch itself spawns under that declaration's worker_identity once it is live. If this session has not already read agent-dispatch's own docs for this, read them now from the installed plugin payload: repository-issue-loop-adoption.md (declaration schema + Operations), repository-issue-loop.md (the full Operations command set + doctor/status diagnosis reference), and README.md's global-recipe table (note: effort-driver-loop has NO dedicated `agent-dispatch effort-driver-loop ...` CLI subcommand group -- it rides the same generic registrar pointer a repository-issue-loop `setup` call already creates for the whole repo). Then, in this exact order -- the adoption doc states `discover` is the side-effect-free check and `setup` (which exposes a declaration to the already-ticking coordinator's cadence) comes only after its output looks right, so run every dry-run BEFORE the one registration call that goes live: (1) for EACH of the three repository-issue-loop declarations, run `discover` (dry-run, works directly against the declaration file, no registration needed) to confirm it sees its real expected GitHub issue(s) before anything can mutate; (2) only once all three look right, register the whole repo with ONE call, `agent-dispatch repository-issue-loop setup <path-to-one-of-the-three-repository-issue-loop-declarations>`, and confirm with `agent-dispatch registrar list`/`discover` that all four declarations (not just the one you named) are now part of the declared profile set; (3) for each of the three repository-issue-loop declarations, run `status`/`doctor` to confirm it is now being served (not overridden off, not missing its pointer); (4) do not hand-trigger any tick yourself -- the already-running local coordinator ticks every declaration on its own declared cadence once registered; wait and periodically re-poll (`agent-dispatch list`, each loop's own `status`/`doctor`) until each of the four loops has produced a real task, and that task has reached a terminal-ish coordinator state (`submitted`, `completed`, `dead_letter`, or `abandoned`) -- or until you have clearly spent a bounded, reasonable amount of real wall-clock time polling (state your own stopping point explicitly rather than polling forever); (5) for each of the four recipes, report the task id, its final coordinator-side status, and the REAL GitHub-side evidence you independently observed with `gh` against this same repo (issue labels/comments, the effort-builder's new/updated effort assignment, the effort-driver's real pull request and the scratch effort's archive state) -- never just restate the task's own self-description; (6) if a loop never produces a task or `doctor` reports a diagnosis, report that diagnosis verbatim (per its documented meaning) rather than guessing or attempting to repair it yourself.

steps: Discover agent-dispatch's own repository-issue-loop docs (adoption + reference) and the README's recipe table, including the explicit effort-driver-loop CLI gap, rather than guessing the lifecycle.

Dry-run `discover` on each of the three repository-issue-loop declarations FIRST (it works directly against the declaration file, no registration needed) to confirm real eligible issues are seen before anything can mutate forge state.

Only once all three dry-runs look right, register the real repo once via `repository-issue-loop setup` on any one of the three forge-backed declarations, then confirm via `registrar list`/`discover` that all four declarations (including the non-forge effort-driver-loop one) are part of the declared profile set from that single registration.
Then `status`/`doctor` each of the three repository-issue-loop declarations to confirm each is now actually being served.
Let the already-running coordinator tick on its own declared cadence (never hand-invent a 'run now' step that doesn't exist) and poll for real task creation and terminal state across all four loops.

Report real, independently-observed GitHub-side evidence (via `gh`) for each of the four recipes, distinct from the task's own self-reported completion, and report a `doctor` diagnosis verbatim for any loop that did not produce a healthy task.
expected_outcome.affirmative_ready: all four loops are confirmed part of the declared profile set from one registration call, and for each of the four recipes the orchestrator reports either a real terminal coordinator task state with corroborating real GitHub-side evidence, or an accurate, verbatim `doctor` diagnosis explaining why no task was produced -- never a guess, a fabricated result, or the orchestrator doing the recipe's own work itself.
expected_outcome.pass_if: the orchestrator discovered and followed the real docs, registered the repo with a single documented call, confirmed all four declarations were picked up, let the real coordinator tick them rather than inventing a manual trigger, and reported accurate terminal state plus real corroborating GitHub-side evidence (or an accurate doctor diagnosis) for each of the four recipes -- without ever acting as a recipe worker itself.
expected_outcome.false_pass_if: the orchestrator itself edits the fixture issues/PRs/effort files to manufacture a 'done' outcome instead of letting agent-dispatch's own spawned headless workers do that work; it fabricates or guesses a task id, status, or GitHub-side evidence instead of reading it for real; it claims a loop succeeded in prose while a real `status`/`doctor` call would show otherwise; it invents a CLI subcommand that does not exist (e.g. an `effort-driver-loop` command group, or a manual 'force tick now' flag) instead of relying on the real registered-profile-set + coordinator-cadence mechanism; or it declares the run complete without ever actually registering the repo via a real `agent-dispatch repository-issue-loop setup` call.
